 Home » Singapore Fintech Festival 2026 » Italy Returns to Singapore Fintech Festival With 7 Startups and SMEs Singapore Fintech Festival 2026 Various Italy Returns to Singapore Fintech Festival With 7 Startups and SMEs
 Italy’s fifth national pavilion brings seven startups and SMEs plus the Bank of Italy, as Rome and Singapore work towards a strategic partnership. Fintech News Singapore November 18, 2026 3 Mins Read LinkedIn Facebook Twitter Telegram Copy Link Email Share LinkedIn Facebook Twitter Copy Link Telegram Email Free Newsletter Get the hottest Fintech Singapore News once a month in your Inbox
 Italy is returning to the Singapore Fintech Festival (SFF) for the fifth consecutive year with a national pavilion organised by the Italian Trade Agency (ITA).
 The participation aims to position Singapore as a gateway to Asia for Italian fintechs and Italy as a launchpad into Europe for Singapore firms.
 The pavilion at Singapore EXPO runs from 18 to 20 November. It features seven Italian startups and SMEs with solutions spanning AI, regtech, payments and digital assets.
 ITA shares the pavilion with the Bank of Italy , ItaliaFintech , the Italian fintech industry association, and two investment promotion bodies, YesMilano and Invest in Lombardy.
 Italy and Singapore work towards strategic partnership 
 Italy and Singapore are working towards a strategic partnership, building on more than six decades of bilateral trade and investment.
 The EU-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement , which has been in force since February 2026, establishes common rules for cross-border data flows and electronic signatures. These provide a foundation for cross-border financial services.
 Dante Brandi “Italy and Singapore want fintech to develop on open, rules-based terms,”
 said Dante Brandi, Ambassador of Italy to Singapore.
 “The Digital Trade Agreement gives our companies a clearer basis to work together, and the strategic partnership our governments are working towards gives that cooperation a long horizon. The task now is to move from exploration to execution, with joint pilots and two-way investment for the decades to come.”
 Opportunities for fintech firms in both markets 
 ITA’s Singapore office helps Italian companies expand into Southeast Asia. SFF provides an opportunity to connect with regional decision-makers across banking, asset management, insurance and venture capital.
 For Singapore fintechs looking towards Europe, ITA points to Italy’s digital payments market, which reached a record €518 billion in 2025.
 Singapore is also committing resources to fintech innovation. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has allocated more than S$220 million over the next three years to support the sector.
 Italy’s presence evolves into national pavilion 
 Italy’s participation at SFF has evolved from individual company showcases into a unified national pavilion.
 Now in its fifth consecutive year, the pavilion brings together seven Italian fintech startups and SMEs alongside institutional representatives.
 The Bank of Italy will present its initiatives to foster innovation and dialogue across the fintech ecosystem.
 Meanwhile, YesMilano and Invest in Lombardy will provide international tech firms with practical market-entry support.
